Class CachedSqlQuery<B>

java.lang.Object
iu.dao.CachedSqlQuery<B>
Type Parameters:
B - materialized row type
All Implemented Interfaces:
ParameterizedSql, SqlQuery<B>, AutoCloseable
final class CachedSqlQuery<B> extends Object implements SqlQuery<B>
A SqlQuery that reads its cursor once, into a list, and answers every accessor from it.

What draining buys, and what it costs

The delegate is read to exhaustion on the first accessor that returns rows, and the complete list is held by the process-wide cache. A generated bean query can also publish its complete mapped rows as individual loads; a raw SQL query deliberately does not, because it may select a partial entity or a value with no entity mapping. This class only replays the query's own list.

The cost is that getResults(int) is no longer lazy. It still pages — each call returns the next maxRows rows and leaves the cursor where it stopped — but the rows behind those pages have already been materialized, so paging bounds what the caller handles at once rather than what the query holds. A query over a result set too large to hold in memory should not be wrapped.

Cursor semantics

The cursor is honored as SqlQuery describes it. Accessors read forward from the current position; getSingleResult(), getFirstRecord() and getResults() are terminal and close; getResults(int) leaves the position where it stopped. Closing rewinds to the first row, and because the rows are already held, reopening replays them rather than re-reading the database — which is what makes this a cache and not merely a buffer.

getResultSet() is the one accessor a list cannot answer, since it hands the caller the driver's own cursor. It bypasses the cached rows and returns a fresh delegate cursor, so a later list accessor reads forward from wherever the caller left that cursor.

    • getResults

      public List<B> getResults(int maxRows)
      Description copied from interface: SqlQuery
      Reads up to maxRows remaining rows, leaving the cursor open so that a subsequent call returns the next page.

      A result smaller than maxRows — including an empty result — means the cursor is exhausted. Because this method never closes, callers must close this query, normally with try-with-resources.

      Specified by:
      getResults in interface SqlQuery<B>
      Parameters:
      maxRows - maximum number of rows to read; must be positive
      Returns:
      up to maxRows results, in cursor order

    • getResultStream

      public Stream<B> getResultStream()
      Description copied from interface: SqlQuery
      Gets a sequential stream over the remaining rows, reading each row from the cursor on demand.

      The stream releases this query's JDBC resources when it is closed and when it reaches the end of the cursor. A stream abandoned before either happens leaves the connection open, so use try-with-resources on the stream or on this query whenever the traversal may end early.

      Specified by:
      getResultStream in interface SqlQuery<B>
      Returns:
      sequential stream over the remaining results

    • getResultSet

      public ResultSet getResultSet()
      Description copied from interface: SqlQuery
      Executes the query if it has not already executed and gets the underlying JDBC result set, for callers that need to read columns directly.

      The result set remains owned by this query and is closed by ParameterizedSql.close(); callers must not close it directly, and must close this query.

      Specified by:
      getResultSet in interface SqlQuery<B>
      Returns:
      open, forward-only result set positioned at the current cursor row

    • getPreparedStatement

      public PreparedStatement getPreparedStatement()
      Description copied from interface: ParameterizedSql
      Opens a connection if one is not already held, prepares the SQL, and binds ParameterizedSql.getArguments().

      Each call discards and closes any statement and connection from a previous call, so the returned reference must not be retained across invocations. The returned statement remains owned by this operation and is closed by ParameterizedSql.close(); callers must not close it directly.

      Specified by:
      getPreparedStatement in interface ParameterizedSql
      Returns:
      prepared JDBC statement, positioned before execution

    • close

      public void close()
      Description copied from interface: ParameterizedSql
      Releases the JDBC resources held by this operation.

      Closing is idempotent and never throws: failures encountered while releasing resources are discarded so that they cannot mask an application failure already in flight. After closing, the operation may be used again, which re-prepares the SQL against a new connection.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
